title: Define SDK client support rubric for enterprise streaming and auth ergonomics
creator: Jordan Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are submitting a steady stream of SDK and client-library requests that span language support gaps, authentication patterns (SSO, KMS integration, short-lived tokens), and streaming ergonomics (partial responses, reconnect semantics). Current intake is ad hoc: PMs, SEs, and engineering triage them differently, leading to inconsistent prioritization and duplicated work across language tracks.

Goal: Create a concise, actionable rubric to triage new SDK/client requests from enterprise customers so we can: 1) decide supported languages and minimal API ergonomics, 2) surface required auth patterns and guardrails, and 3) classify streaming feature requests by compatibility, risk, and implementation effort. The rubric should feed into backlog scoring and trigger follow-up playbooks (e.g., enterprise onboarding, security review, dedicated support).

Scope: Non-bug feature requests only. Focus on: language bindings, auth patterns (SSO/SAML, short-lived credentials, KMS support), streaming ergonomics (client reconnect, resume, partial chunking, backpressure), and recipe-level docs (examples, migration notes). Not in scope: core runtime scheduling, infra capacity buys, or model behavior changes.

Deliverables: 1) A triage rubric doc with scoring categories (customer priority, security surface, engineering effort, cross-language complexity, maintenance burden) and recommended actions for each score band; 2) a playbook for handling enterprise auth requests (checklist for KMS, audit log requirements, legal notes); 3) recommended minimum SDK surface for language adoption (core APIs, streaming API contract, error model); 4) sample prioritization of 6 recent customer requests to validate rubric.

Acceptance criteria: Rubric reviewed by Eng (runtime + SDK owners), Security, and Solutions Engineering; rubric reduces average triage time by >30% in a 2-week pilot; at least 2 enterprise requests are advanced to scoping or scheduled release using the rubric.
